messages.author: a0c9c53065dc7f03
messages.subject: GGIR 2.9.0 ID errors
parts:
Hi Vincent,

I found the IDs are not used correctly in part4 sleep reports, for example,

EVISX3          ELP29O__034637_2017-12-01 09-09-28.bin.RData   EVISX3    sleeplog
 
 The ID was ELP29O in the old GGIR version. Please kindly advise me if I could still use GGIR2.9.0 outputs. Hope you never merge the data using ID and use filename as the only link to do the data merge.

By the way,  I found out that GGIR use the later sleep period since this data includes two separate 14 days observation in 2017 and 2019, but part2 activity data use the earlier period in 2017. This leads to no overlap in part2 and part4.  In GGIR2.2, I do not have this issue since both parts use the earlier period in 2017.

Please kindly advise. I have sent this sample by email yesterday.

Thank you so much.
Best,
Wei

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GGIR 2.9.0 ID errors
parts:
Hi Wei,

It may be easier if I reply in this thread again to your message from earlier today in the other thread.

I see that the .RData file you sent refers in its filename to "ELP29O__034637_2017-12-01 09-09-28.bin", but inside the file I see that the content represents file "EVISX3__034650_2019-07-22 10-38-07.bin". This explains why it cannot match with the sleeplog because ID EVISX3 is not in the sleep diary.

So, I think you will need to reprocess the bin files to make sure that their output corresponds to the filenames it is stored as. Possibly this relates to the same bug I fixed earlier this year in the processing of data stored in subfolders.

Best,
Vincent

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GGIR 2.9.0 ID errors
parts:
Hi Wei,

To follow-up on my previous message, it may be good to elaborate a bit more on the reason why this was a bug:

GGIR originally sorted the full path to the filenames and the filenames only before processing them. This is no problem when all files are in the same folder, but becomes a problem when working with folder names that influence the ordering.

Example 1:

folderA/file1
folderA/file2
folderB/file3
folderB/file4
This will order to: file1, file2, file3, file 4. All is good because that is also what we get when we simply order the filenames without path.

Example 2:

folderA/file3
folderA/file4
folderB/file1
folderB/file2
This will reorder to file3, file4, file1, file 2. This is not good, because filename ordering is different from full path ordering.

To address this I removed all ordering of filenames in GGIR and left the ordering all the way to the end just at the report creation step.

Best,

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GGIR 2.9.0 ID errors
parts:
Hi Wei,

Inside the .bin file header the ID is stored as ELP290 (last character zero), which is what GGIR uses but struggles to match with ELP29O (last character letter O) in the sleeplog.

So, I think the error is a 0/O typo in the ID number, which may be the result of a similar typo in the bin filename: ELP29O__034637_2017-12-01 09-09-28.bin

To me seems like a manipulation of the filename after you last processed the file successfully and not a GGIR bug, could that be?

Best,

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GGIR 2.9.0 ID errors
parts: Dear Wei,
I do not know how to manipulate the bin file and I do not think I can do it.

It is not the file itself but the name of the file. Someone changed the number zero to a letter O in the filename. I know this because the GENEActiv software always stores the ID as entered in both the filename and the fileheader.

When setting argument idloc=1, GGIR tries to use the ID from the file header, while when idloc=2 (or any other number) GGIR aims to extract the ID from the filename. This has been the case for a long time, even long before the 2.2-0 release in 2020. In the script "BATS_ggir0.callpipeline.R" you sent me you have argument idloc = 1, which indicates that you were telling GGIR to extract the ID from the file header.

If this worked in the past, then the fact that it worked was a bug, because it should not have worked when ID log in the file header is not consistent with the ID in the sleeplog. Possibly the bug was the subfolder bug I mentioned before that linked the wrong ID to the wrong filename.

An alternative explanation is that you used idloc = 2 in the past and changed it to 1, but I trust that you would be aware of such change.

A third explanation is that someone change the ID in the sleep diary not realising that it is not the ID in the accelerometer file name that is used when idloc = 1 but the ID in the file header.

Either way, the solution is to not set idloc = 1 when you do not trust the ID in the file header. I just tested this with idloc=2 on your file and it works: GGIR produces the attached part 4 reports.

Best,

Vincent

On Mon, Jun 5, 2023 at 3:54 AM Vincent van Hees <v.va...@accelting.com> wrote:
Dear Wei,

I do not know how to manipulate the bin file and I do not think I can do it.

It is not the file itself but the name of the file. Someone changed the number zero to a letter O in the filename. I know this because the GENEActiv software always stores the ID as entered in both the filename and the fileheader.

When setting argument idloc=1, GGIR tries to use the ID from the file header, while when idloc=2 (or any other number) GGIR aims to extract the ID from the filename. This has been the case for a long time, even long before the 2.2-0 release in 2020. In the script "BATS_ggir0.callpipeline.R" you sent me you have argument idloc = 1, which indicates that you were telling GGIR to extract the ID from the file header.

If this worked in the past, then the fact that it worked was a bug, because it should not have worked when ID log in the file header is not consistent with the ID in the sleeplog. Possibly the bug was the subfolder bug I mentioned before that linked the wrong ID to the wrong filename.

An alternative explanation is that you used idloc = 2 in the past and changed it to 1, but I trust that you would be aware of such change.

A third explanation is that someone change the ID in the sleep diary not realising that it is not the ID in the accelerometer file name that is used when idloc = 1 but the ID in the file header.

Either way, the solution is to not set idloc = 1 when you do not trust the ID in the file header. I just tested this with idloc=2 on your file and it works: GGIR produces the attached part 4 reports.

Best,

Vincent

I see that the .RData file you sent refers in its filename to "ELP29O__034637_2017-12-01 09-09-28.bin", but inside the file I see that the content represents file "EVISX3__034650_2019-07-22 10-38-07.bin".
